architecture.mechanism: An edible xanthan-gum film (0.5% xanthan + 1% glycerol + 2% citric acid) acts as a barrier to gas/moisture exchange while serving as a carrier for live probiotic lactobacillus strains that provide in-situ biopreservation (antimicrobial metabolites competitive exclusion of spoilage flora), with citric acid in the matrix inhibiting polyphenol oxidase, jointly suppressing microbial spoilage and enzymatic browning.
architecture.intervention: Dip fresh-cut mango cubes for ~1-2 min in a food-grade solution of 0.5% xanthan gum, 1% glycerol, and 2% citric acid inoculated with Lactiplantibacillus plantarum (and/or Bifidobacterium longum) at ~8.0 log CFU/mL, drain, and pack in low-cost passive film (no MAP, no refrigeration, no chemical preservatives) for 25 C distribution.
architecture.expected_effect: Reduced total aerobic/yeast-mold counts and delayed browning, better retention of color, ascorbic acid, carotenoids and total phenols, with shelf life extended from 5 days toward 21 days at 25 C at an estimated added cost well under 0.05 USD/kg (xanthan, glycerol, citric acid are bulk food-grade ingredients; probiotic culture cost is minimal at dip concentrations).
architecture.falsification_test: Run a matched 25 C storage trial (0, 5, 10, 15, 21 days) comparing uncoated control, xanthan-citric coating without probiotics, and the full probiotic-xanthan coating, measuring microbial counts (total aerobic, yeasts/molds, lactobacilli), color L*/b* and browning index, PPO activity, ascorbic acid, and sensory acceptance; the mechanism is falsified if the probiotic coating fails to keep microbial load and browning index significantly below the control beyond day 5, or if any treatment fails to reach 21 days at acceptable quality, or if ingredient/culture cost exceeds 0.05 USD/kg.
